lib/safety.ts: // ips-v6, read 2026-10-25). Workers cannot open sockets to them, so a page
// behind Cloudflare's proxy is requested with fetch() instead.
lib/tls.ts: // Reads which certificate authority issued a site's certificate, from the
// start of one TLS 1.2 handshake: a ClientHello, then the server's
// Certificate message, which TLS 1.2 sends unencrypted (TLS 1.3 encrypts
// it, so a server that speaks only 1.3 gives no answer). The connection is
// closed once the certificates arrive; no key exchange, no HTTP request.
// Runtime-neutral: the Worker feeds it a cloudflare:sockets connection.
scripts/dev.ts: // The local Workers runtime trusts the system's CA file, which on macOS lacks
// newer roots such as GlobalSign Root R46, so https to sites under them fails
// as "cannot connect". Give it the current Mozilla roots that ship with Bun.
// Deployed, the Worker uses Cloudflare's trust store instead.
worker/certs.ts: // Workers cannot open sockets to Cloudflare's addresses; visitors of a
// proxied site get Cloudflare's certificate there, not the origin's.
worker/php.ts: // A cross-site form can send text/plain without a preflight; requiring
// JSON means another site's page cannot make a visitor's browser call us.
worker/pinned.ts: // The page request on Cloudflare's TCP sockets, which (unlike fetch()) adds no
// CF-Worker header for a site's firewall to refuse. Plain http connects to the
// address safeTransport checked, so DNS is not consulted again and a name that
// answers differently a second time cannot redirect it. https connects to the
// name, whose certificate the handshake checks (see safeTransport).
